source.via: Gros 2017 restates Zubrin-Andrews only partly: the bow-shock pressure balance (his eq. (31), citing [13]), 'a powerlaw scaling [13] such as A_V ~ (v/c)^alpha', the Andrews-Zubrin 1990 axial value A(v)~75 vs Gros 18 at the same parameters, and Z-A's 'I = 159e3 A and v = c/10' case. Zubrin-Andrews 1991's own drag formula and coefficient are NAMED-NOT-READ here; nothing in this report quotes them. Gros's own momentum-braking law (eqs (1),(8)-(14),(16),(19),(20)) is READ in full.

published_statement: Gros 2017 (READ): eq. (1) 'd/dt(m_tot v) = -(A(v) n_p v)(2 m_p v)' for fully reflected incoming particles; eq. (8) 'A(v) = A_c [log(I/(beta I_c))]^3, v < (cI)/I_c' with A_c = 0.081 pi R^2 and I_c = 1.55e6 A, fitted to non-relativistic Lorentz-force trajectory integrations (eq. (4)) 'over two orders of magnitude'; A(v) 'vanishes altogether when I < beta I_c' ('we cannot resolve numerically whether A(v) really vanishes ... or drops to finite but exceedingly small values'); eq. (11) finite stopping distance x_max = (1/0.081) log^-2(v0 I_c/(cI)) m_tot/(4 m_p n_p pi R^2); eq. (19) at optimal current x_max = 3.1 m_tot/(m_p n_p pi R^2). On Zubrin-Andrews: 'previous estimates [13] ... have been rather on the optimistic side'; 'a powerlaw scaling [13] such as A_V ~ (v/c)^alpha would be inconsistent with the existence of a critical current I_c'; Z-A's I = 159e3 A at v = c/10 'would be right on the point where protons are not reflected at all'. Restated Z-A bow-shock pressure balance (Gros eq. (31)): n_p m_p v^2/2 = (2B)^2/(2 mu0) ~ 2 B0^2 R^6/(mu0 z^6), 'clearly only a rough estimate'.
published_hypotheses: Gros: momentum transfer to CHARGED particles only -- 'reflecting the H+ ions of the interstellar medium'; n_p is the ionized-proton density, 0.05-0.20 cm^-3 in the warm local clouds and ~0.005 cm^-3 in the Local Bubble (Sect. 2.1)
Gros: limit of independent particles (low density); bow-shock formation only touched in Appendix B and found 'only marginally compatible'
Gros: non-relativistic Lorentz force m_p dv/dt = q v x B (eq. 4); results scale with v/I
Gros: axial configuration (loop field parallel to v); idealized sail; thermal motion of ISM protons neglected (effective area shrinks when thermal and craft speeds are comparable)
Gros: full reflection factor 2 m_p v per reflected proton (eq. 1); effective area defined by eq. (7) A = 2 pi int (1-S(r))/2 r dr
Gros: A(v) velocity dependent, zero above beta = I/I_c; equals the bare loop area only at I/beta = 15.6e6 A
Z-A 1991 as restated by Gros: plasma-fluid (MHD) bow shock with magnetic/kinetic pressure balance; a power-law effective area A ~ (v/c)^alpha (exponent not given in the restatement)

rederivation.outcome: 25/25 checks ok, exit 0 (output in rederive/magsail-drag-law.out). (1) Tree's arithmetic reproduced: 2001.638 AU; table 8.42/0.08/0.00 ly; the prose pair (810 AU, 2.6 ly) needs two areas 76x apart -- discrepancy recorded. (2) Constant-A v^2 drag solved exactly: v = v0 exp(-rho A x/m); no finite distance to rest; at the tree's L the ship keeps 60.7% of its speed (37% of KE); 0.0476 c -> 100 km/s needs 19,826 AU = 9.9x the floor. So 'floor' is true under the tree's own hypothesis. (3) Relativistic constant-A, closed forms verified by differentiation: with the tree's force (gamma^3/beta) or the covariant ram drag (gamma/beta), 0.866c->0.0476c needs 4.19 or 3.19 m/(rho A) vs the tree's 1.333; both diverge at beta->0 -- floor holds. (4) Pressure balance (Gros eq. 31): z ~ v^(-1/3), F ~ v^(4/3), finite stopping distance = exactly 3x the energy/initial-drag estimate. (5) Gros eq. (10) verified to solve eqs (1)+(8) symbolically; x_max/L_tree = a/2 (A read as A(v0)) or 6.17/a^2 (A read as bare area); Gros's own printed numbers reproduce: eq.(13) 0.91/0.98, eq.(14) tau = 1.840 and 5.246 (printed 1.84, 5.2), eq.(16) 4.2e6, eq.(19) 3.1, eq.(20) 0.37 and 8.44 ly. (6) Gros law on the tree's case: 12,335 AU at n=1; the 0.866c row needs I > 1.34e6 A and lies outside the non-relativistic model; Z-A's I = 159 kA at c/10 sits within 3% of Gros's cutoff (1.55e5 A), as Gros states. One transcription error of MINE (sign of the x term of Gros eq. (10)) failed the first run and was corrected against the source's '(x0 - x)'; not a source error.

later_literature.what: Single-particle Biot-Savart simulations for dilute media: effective area velocity dependent (log^3 law) with a hard critical-current cutoff; finite stopping distance; Z-A's estimates 'rather on the optimistic side' (A = 18 vs Andrews-Zubrin's 75 at identical parameters, source of discrepancy 'unclear'); Z-A's c/10, 159 kA case sits at the no-reflection point. Narrows the tree's constant-A law and excludes the 0.87 c row absent ~MA currents; does not refute momentum braking.

lacked_data: What Zubrin-Andrews (1990/1991) lacked, as far as READ here: (i) particle-level simulations of proton reflection by a current loop in the dilute (independent-particle) limit -- supplied by Gros 2017, which finds a velocity-dependent area with a critical-current cutoff and an area 4x smaller than Andrews-Zubrin's at identical parameters, and says the source of the discrepancy is 'unclear'; (ii) the current census of the local ISM ion density (Crawford 2011: 0.05-0.21 cm^-3 locally, 0.005-0.04 in the Local Bubble). Does having it change the conclusion? Evidence either way: it does NOT overturn the momentum-braking framework -- Gros reaches finite stopping distances and a feasible 1.5 t slow Trappist-1 mission with it; it DOES change the magnitudes: a constant-A, n = 1 cm^-3, coefficient-1 floor (the tree's) is not a brake distance, and with Gros's law at the tree's own mass and speed the full stop takes 12,335 AU at n=1 and ~123,000 AU (1.95 ly) at the LIC's n_p = 0.1 -- against the tree's printed 810 AU. At 0.87 c the later data cut the other way from M's hypothesis: no source model covers it at all (non-relativistic, cutoff), so the tree's high-beta row is unsupported rather than refuted, and its own verdict 'ISM braking is a low-beta technology' survives. The Z-A-vs-Gros effective-area disagreement is a live model discrepancy, not a refutation of Z-A (whose paper is unread here).
grade_evidence: The tree's law F = rho v^2 A (coefficient 1, constant A, total proton density) is a generic ram-drag form, internally correct for its stated hypotheses: its arithmetic reproduces (2001.638 AU), and its 'floor' label is TRUE under its own constant-A hypothesis (exact solution v = v0 e^(-rho A x/m): no finite stop; relativistic forms also diverge) and under the pressure-balance scaling (true distance = 3L). But every READ magsail law holds on a smaller class than the tree uses: the effective area is velocity dependent (Gros eq. 8; pressure balance z ~ v^-1/3), momentum transfer is to ions only (0.05-0.21 cm^-3 locally, not 1), full reflection carries a factor 2, and the physics is non-relativistic with A = 0 unless I > beta*1.55e6 A -- so the 0.87 c row is outside every source's domain. Under Gros's law the 'floor' label itself depends on reading A: it holds if A is the bare loop area (x_max = 6.17 L at a=1) and fails if A is the initial effective area (x_max = 0.5 L at a=1). Not WRONG: no published statement is refuted and no computed contradiction of the tree's formula under its own hypotheses exists; the 810 AU / 2.6 ly vs 2001.64 AU / 0.084 ly mismatch is a tree-internal discrepancy, recorded not graded. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: the ion density has not moved since 2011 (the tree drops the hypothesis rather than using a superseded datum), and Z-A-vs-Gros is a model disagreement the tree does not use.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: a READ source giving magsail drag with constant effective area and coefficient 1 against total (neutral+ion) density, valid to 0.87 c -- none found. To WRONG: a computed contradiction of the tree's floor under its OWN hypotheses (none: the constant-A floor is proven to hold), or a READ result showing momentum braking cannot stop a craft at 0.048 c at any area. To OPEN: if the cached 1707.02801v3 text were shown not to be the published text. Reading Zubrin-Andrews 1991 directly (its drag formula and coefficient) and a post-2018 relativistic/kinetic magsail study (e.g. PIC) could narrow further or shift the coefficient; a relativistic reflection model would decide the 0.87 c row, which no READ source covers.
